page: Amazon Web Services r8g.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by custom 64-bit ARM-based AWS Graviton processors. Specifically, it features the AWS Neoverse-V2 CPU running at 2.8 GHz with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, utilizing a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance, with a Passmark memory score in the top 25% and a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 462.02 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs in the top 25% at 14.39 GB/sec. However, general CPU compute benchmarks show moderate to lower performance; the Passmark CPU score falls in the bottom 25%, and the CPU encryption test is in the bottom 10%. Redis SET operations average 8.53 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 10.25 GB/sec.

The r8g.xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a resource-dense option for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of high-frequency compute costs. The lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage, and the baseline network speed is limited to 2 Gbps. Given the strong memory bandwidth and average database performance, this instance is suited for caching layers like Redis, medium-sized databases, and memory-bound data processing tasks, while it is less optimal for heavy cryptographic operations or large-scale LLM inference.
